children: Tesla
and The Walt Disney Company
both received notable upgrades, with analysts seeing significant potential in autonomous mobility and improved entertainment fundamentals, respectively. On the other side, Microsoft
and Nike
both received downgrades, with analysts citing concerns over capital expenditure efficiency and near-term selling pressure.
Upgrades
The Walt Disney Company
: Upgrade Hold to Buy by
The analyst cites strong Q3 performance with 7% YoY revenue growth and 21% segment operating income growth, along with an attractive valuation at a 36% discount to its five-year average forward P/E.
"With cash being king, Disney seems to be in pretty good shape. Their operating cash flows grew even quicker than operating income as a signal of strong cash generation. YoY, the company's

, and this, of course, helped to drive the surge in FCFs. For investors, this is good news, particularly since Disney increased share buybacks from $711 million in the year ago quarter to $1.745 billion. This might also indicate that the company itself believes its stock is undervalued."
Tesla
: Upgrade to Buy by

The analyst cites Tesla's launch of its camera-only Cybercab robotaxi in Austin as a pivotal move toward disrupting the potential $1.4 trillion robotaxi market, though regulatory hurdles and geographic limitations remain significant challenges.
"Many, including former PayPal

co-founder Peter Thiel (also a billionaire), have stated that it’s folly to bet against the world’s most outstanding tech entrepreneur and wealthiest individual. If an aggressively oriented investor can accept risk is always present, even for Musk, Tesla is a Buy."
Downgrades
Microsoft
: Downgrade Strong Buy to Hold by Aseity Research.

The analyst notes that despite Azure repositioning away from OpenAI, capital expenditure remains heavily weighted toward GPUs and CPUs, depressing free cash flow while the current valuation already reflects OpenAI growth expectations.

"I'm downgrading my rating to 'Hold' because a 'Strong Buy' thesis requires an obvious or high-conviction mispricing, and I don't see either. When the stock was still $394 and the OpenAI rewrite looked not yet priced in, it earned a table-pounding 'Strong Buy,' which paid off. At $499~ though, the OpenAI unwinding process is already in the price. The rest of the story for Microsoft needs to be earned and is not worth paying for in advance. So I am not selling, but I am also not adding shares either."
Nike
: Downgrade Buy to Hold by Elina Selianska.

The analyst points to near-term technical selling pressure following S&P 100 exclusion and a slower-than-expected operational turnaround to wholesale, despite intact long-term brand strength and gross margins.

"Current problems arose completely not because consumers suddenly hated the Nike brand. People still buy and wear their sneakers all over the world. The problem hides in a broken distribution pipe and a self-inflicted marketing wound. This is a severe illness. But it is exactly not terminal."
